intro.title: React Router Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a simple multi-page navigation app using React Router. You'll learn how to set up routes to display different components based on the URL path. The core concept is client-side routing, which allows navigation without full page reloads. You'll use key constructs like BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, and Link. By the end, you'll have a functional app that switches between pages smoothly.
intro.usecase: React Router is the standard library for handling navigation in single-page applications (SPAs), enabling seamless transitions between different views without full page reloads. You'll use it to build product dashboards where users click between analytics, user management, and settings panels, or e-commerce sites where shoppers browse categories, view product details, and check out—all within the same app. As a developer, implementing React Router allows you to create clean, bookmarkable URLs and manage complex nested layouts, like admin interfaces with sidebars and modals, mirroring real-world apps from social media feeds to banking portals.
